question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & -2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Which of the following is a basis of the eigenspace corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-2?$
question.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =-2.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & -2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}]-(-2)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}=0 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -10 & -10 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=-{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get 

$$
{x}_{1}+2(-{x}_{3})+2{x}_{3}=0\,⇒\,{x}_{1}=0.
$$

So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Therefore, the required basis is 

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}.
$$
